structure: A single short Markdown ruling file, 117 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-06.md), from Ian, dated 6 November 2026, settling transporter management, which ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements. It is laid out as a preamble of verbatim block quotes then four headed lists. The preamble (lines 1-26) names the block being lifted and quotes the owner in six blockquotes: four on who manages transporters and the mid-journey pattern and approved transporters, then, under a second lead-in, two quoting the questions put back to the owner about the data model, the collection, roles and how Northern Ireland is held. "## Decided" (lines 27-80) rules in six numbered points, each marked "New.": the address book as system of record, the mid-journey hand-off, approved transporters parked (with a further verbatim quote from later the same day clarifying that the eight shipped records are the approved transporters and the increment movements that follow), the transporter as its own document in its own transporters collection, no roles but a private-or-commercial type, and a commercial transporter's country forced to XI with no reference-data lookup. "## Follows from the decision, for the re-distil to work through" (lines 82-105) holds five numbered consequences, 7 to 11, which the file says are not separate rulings but what the decisions mean for code already on main, each left to the re-distil to settle against the real services. "## Still open" (lines 107-110) holds one point, 12. "## Unchanged" (lines 112-117) holds one point, 13, on the Northern Ireland address search staying blocked on its own blocker. Scope is the whole file and nothing in it is left out; it is small enough for one agent to read word for word, so it is one part.

parts.title: Whole ruling
parts.scope: The whole file, lines 1 to 117: the preamble and its six block quotes, the six numbered points under "Decided" with point 3's later clarification quote, the five consequences 7 to 11 under "Follows from the decision", the single open point 12 under "Still open", and point 13 under "Unchanged". There is no other part.
covers: The preamble: that this settles what ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 and claim c-285 left blocked — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does — and the four quotes that rule it: the address book will manage transporters saved per organisation, the same mid-journey address book pattern is used when adding transporters, the previous ruling was based on the 'approved transporters' concept possibly managed in MDM for all organisations, and 'Don't worry about the approved transporters for now'

The two quotes at lines 20-26 that are questions put to the owner (whether transporters need the same data model, whether they can live in the address book service in a different collection, whether they need the same roles, and whether MDM is used for a Northern Ireland country lookup or a commercial transporter is just forced to a Northern Ireland country code) — recorded as the questions they are, with the decisions taken from the Decided points that answer them, never from the question wording alone

Decided point 1: the address book manages transporters, a transporter is a record held per organisation exactly as every other address is, trade-imports-address-book is the system of record, this supersedes ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 and claim c-285, and it settles for transporters the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-093 left to 'follow the real services'

Decided point 2: adding a transporter mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses — the INS front door's add pages opened in journey mode, landing back in the journey on save or cancel, the same pattern as inc-077, inc-078 and inc-080 (EUDPA-706, merged e1237ac7) — and not a second pattern of its own

Decided point 3: approved transporters are parked — an MDM-managed list for every organisation added on top of an organisation's own transporters is not in scope now, nothing is built for it, and it is recorded as the likely subject of the 9 October block

Decided point 3's clarification later the same day, with its verbatim quote: the eight records services/transporters/records.js ships to every organisation are the approved transporters in an initial hardcoded form and are parked with the rest; they stay exactly as they are, main's two commercial placeholders are not replaced with Design Release 2.1's four, and the private records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed; Design Release 2.1's records (req-397, req-398) and picking one of those eight move off inc-037 to inc-265 with the list question (req-2172); inc-037 still builds the list over whatever the organisation itself has added, held by the address book under decision 1

Decided point 4: a transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address data model — its own document, controller, repository and route, beside addresses, reusing the service's organisation scoping (IdentityHeaderFilter), soft-delete status, optimistic locking and Standard Address Block field validation where the fields are genuinely the same; the address book's own API is unchanged, AddressRequest requiring at least one role (@NotEmpty) and refusing a type outright (@Null, 'type is not a supported field'), neither of which a transporter can satisfy; and a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has

Decided point 5: transporters have no roles and have a type instead — AddressRole exists to say which records a picker may offer for a slot, to drive the receiving-roles-in-the-United-Kingdom rule and the list's three category tabs; a transporter is never one of those six roles and has one use (the transporter step), so no seventh role and no fourth role group is added; the private-or-commercial type is stored instead because it is intrinsic, deciding the form, the field list and the country rule, and so unlike an address's type (dropped by ruling:paul-2026-11-05 as derivable from roles) it cannot be derived; and the INS front door's Transporter tab is a fourth tab backed by the transporters route, not a fourth role group over addresses

Decided point 6: a commercial transporter's country is forced to XI with no reference-data lookup — it is not a choice, the add form fixes the country, posts it in a hidden field and refuses a tampered value rather than correcting it (c-055); MDM could not serve it, its country list being the origin and export list of 249 entries with no United Kingdom at all, which is why addressCountries() prepends GB/United Kingdom in code; the code persisted is XI, displayed as 'Northern Ireland', both held as constants in the service; XI is this estate's existing Northern Ireland code, trade-imports-schemas' DOCOM samples carrying "countryId": "XI" with "countryName": "United Kingdom (Northern Ireland)" against Belfast BT postcodes; being distinct from GB it keeps 'must be Northern Ireland' enforceable from the stored value alone with no postcode parsing and no extra flag, and keeps a transporter's country the same type as the address book's countryCode rather than today's display string; and a private transporter is unaffected, keeping its choice of country from the United Kingdom plus reference-data's export countries (inc-008)

The lead-in to "Follows from the decision": these are not separate rulings but what the decisions above mean for code already on main, and the re-distil of the transporter area should settle each against the real services — so each of points 7 to 11 is claimed for what it states about today's code and what it leaves to the re-distil, not as a fresh decision

Point 7: the animals frontend's transporter store is not the system of record — services/transporters/register.js keeps added transporters in an in-memory Map per process, lost on restart and not shared between instances; under decision 1 the address book replaces it, and inc-039's requirement that added transporters 'stay on its list for later notifications' becomes real persistence rather than the current demo-grade capture

Point 8: the add pages' home follows decision 2 — the INS front door beside the other address add pages, rather than features/transport/transporter-add, .../private-transporter-details and .../commercial-transporter-details in the animals frontend; what becomes of those three folders is the re-distil's to decide

Point 9: inc-074, inc-075 and inc-076 become the primary route rather than an extra one, the Transporter option on 'Choose an address type' now has somewhere to lead, and which of the two placements still in play it takes — req-1198's third before 'Branch', or req-2042's after 'Place of Destination' and before the divider — is settled at the re-distil against the three-option page inc-061 built

Point 10: a transporter's approval status (Approved or New, shown on the list) is not the address book's AddressStatus, which is an ACTIVE or DELETED soft-delete tombstone, so with the two on one service the transporter document needs its own name for its own concept

Point 11: decision 6 makes the commercial transporter's stored country a code rather than today's display string 'Northern Ireland', so the re-distil should say what happens to records captured before the change, if any outlive it
Still open, point 12: which approved-transporter list the list's commercial records come from (req-2172, inc-265) stays open, parked with decision 3 — recorded as a gap claim

Unchanged, point 13: the Northern Ireland address search (inc-042) stays blocked on its own independent blocker, the INS address lookup being still only the EUDPA-390 spike gated to dev and local and not wired in; it waits with the address book's inc-072 and inc-081, which wait on the same thing; and under decision 6 its BT-postcode filter is a search convenience, not the source of truth for the country
Any other open point the ruling leaves on something it touches, recorded as a gap claim with an empty quote
